source_book: Survey Curious? Start-Up Guide — Bergman, Chinco, Hartzmark, Sussman (2020)

test_cases.prompt: I'm using one item to measure investor risk preference. Is that enough?
test_cases.expected_behavior: Activate converging-evidence-design. Default: no. Recommend at least two items using different elicitation methods. State-vs-revealed, recall-vs-infer are common pairs.

test_cases.prompt: How do I make my survey result more robust to wording concerns?
test_cases.expected_behavior: Activate converging-evidence-design. Convergence via re-elicit using a different method. State-vs-choice, abstract-vs-concrete, recall-vs-infer.

test_cases.prompt: I want to ask the same thing two different ways to see if respondents answer consistently.
test_cases.expected_behavior: Activate converging-evidence-design. Recommend two items using DIFFERENT elicitation methods (not two slightly-different wordings). The point is method diversity, not redundancy. Specify state-vs-choice or recall-vs-infer pattern.

test_cases.prompt: I want to make my Likert-agreement item shorter.
test_cases.expected_behavior: Do NOT activate converging-evidence-design. This is a brevity question, not a multi-item one. Defer to clarity-concreteness or experimental-design.
test_cases.notes: Trap: 'one item' could conceivably trigger 'add another'; but if the question is brevity, skip.

test_cases.prompt: Should I run a pilot before launching my survey?
test_cases.expected_behavior: Do NOT activate converging-evidence-design. This is operational flow. Defer to pilot-protocol.
test_cases.notes: Trap: 'pilot' might intersect with multi-item testing; but pilot is the operational vehicle, not item design.

test_cases.prompt: How do I interpret my survey result, given I have only one item per construct?
test_cases.expected_behavior: Do NOT activate converging-evidence-design as the primary response. The user already has data; the right skill is relative-vs-absolute (interpretation). converging-evidence-design can advise 'add another item next time' as a fix-forward comment, but the immediate question is interpretation.
test_cases.notes: Trap: 'one item per construct' phrasing pulls in this skill; but post-collection, the user needs interpretation help.

test_cases.prompt: I'm measuring investor attention with two Likert-agreement scales that say the same thing in slightly different words. Is this converging evidence?
test_cases.expected_behavior: Edge: NO. Two same-method items with similar wording are redundancy, not convergence. Push back: the second item needs a *different elicitation method* (e.g., a recall task, an inference question, a behavioral measure). Explain the principle.
test_cases.notes: Edge: well-intentioned but wrong application of the principle.

notes: Trickiest false-fire: when the user says 'one item per construct', the post-collection version is an interpretation problem (relative-vs-absolute), not a design problem. Filter on 'designing vs. interpreting'.
